The constraints force a unique schedule, and it matches my earlier answer.

Hana, Dev and Elif must occupy three consecutive slots k, k+1, k+2. Hana < Dev < Elif, and exactly one person sits between Elif and Hana, so Dev is that person.

Ann is 2 from Dev, so Ann is at k−1 or k+3. Ann at k−1 forces Cara to k−3, which puts Finn before Elif, a contradiction. So Ann is at k+3, Cara at k+5 (k+1 is Dev), Finn at k+4, and Gus at k+6 (k+2 is Elif).

Ivo and Ben must both come before Gus, so the block k..k+6 needs at least two slots before it. Only k=3 works, which leaves slots 1 and 2 for Ivo and Ben, with Ivo first.

Checking all 13 constraints against the schedule: all pass. Ann (6) and Ben (2) are 4 apart, and Elif (5) and Gus (9) are 4 apart.
